calls.head: Boeser’s line gets the soft minutes
calls.body: At home, the Canucks keep sending Boeser’s line (Cotter, Chytil and Boeser) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Manny Malhotra has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Red Wings’ second line is Brandsegg-Nygård, Finnie and DeBrincat.

calls.plain: The Red Wings’ power play created at least its usual chances. Detroit went 1 for 4 on the power play.
calls.said: the Red Wings’ power play would get its usual chances against the Canucks’ shaky kill
calls.beyond: Detroit has one of the league’s most dangerous power plays, and Vancouver has one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a big night: Detroit’s power play created 16.7 expected goals per 60, against their usual 8.9 (about 10.2 against Vancouver) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: Detroit buried Vancouver in shots
surprises.body: Vancouver gets outshot more than almost anyone. Even by those standards, this was lopsided: Detroit took 56 of the 84 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, Detroit would expect about 58%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: The Red Wings keep the Canucks winless in nine
paras: J.T. Compher was back in the lineup after missing seven games, and picked up an assist. It was a busy first period. Lucas Raymond and William Wallinder scored less than two minutes apart early in the period to put the Red Wings up 2-0. Elias Pettersson (#40) got the Canucks on the board on the power play 58 seconds later. Raymond scored again on the power play just under two minutes later to make it 3-1 for the Wings. Michael Rasmussen stretched the lead to 4-1 late in the second. Michal Postava took over from John Gibson in net for Detroit to start the third. Emmitt Finnie made it 5-1 for the Red Wings early in the third, but Jonathan Lekkerimäki made a dent in Detroit’s lead midway through the period, bringing it to 5-2. Raymond added an assist for a three-point night.

The Red Wings drove the play, outshooting the Canucks 31-13, and the scoreboard caught up. Kevin Lankinen allowed five goals on 31 shots for the Canucks. The Red Wings moved to 4-3-3. The Canucks are winless in nine (0-8-1).

items.text: The Red Wings have points in six straight games (3-0-3).
The Red Wings have beaten the Canucks four straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
Michael Rasmussen scored his first goal of the season, his first since Jan 5 (34 games played since).
Axel Sandin-Pellikka was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Anton Johansson played instead.
